title: HEDIS, eCQMs & the Quality Measurement Ecosystem
summary: The landscape of quality measures — who creates them, how they are reported, what HEDIS and eCQMs are, and the ongoing debate about measure burden and meaningful measurement.

objectives.text: Distinguish between HEDIS measures and eCQMs and how each is collected
Identify the major measure stewards and their roles
Explain why measure burden has become a major issue and what CMS is doing about it

content_blocks.body: Healthcare quality measurement involves multiple organizations creating, endorsing, and reporting measures — often with different methodologies, data sources, and populations. The result is a measurement ecosystem that is rich in data but fragmented in practice.
content_blocks.heading: The measurement ecosystem

items.body: National Committee for Quality Assurance. Creates HEDIS measures — the most widely used quality measures in the US, reported by health plans for their populations.
items.title: NCQA

items.body: Operates the eCQM (electronic clinical quality measure) program, the Hospital Compare reporting system, and ties measures to payment in VBC programs.
items.title: CMS

items.body: National Quality Forum. Endorses measures through a consensus process — NQF endorsement is required for many federal quality programs.
items.title: NQF

items.body: ACC, ACS, AHA and others create specialty-specific registry measures that complement HEDIS and eCQMs for cardiology, oncology, etc.
items.title: Specialty societies

content_blocks.body: Physicians now spend an estimated 15+ hours per week on documentation and reporting requirements. Studies show that every patient visit generates 2+ hours of EHR time. CMS has acknowledged the problem and has been actively sunsetting low-value measures, aligning measure sets across programs, and investing in digital quality measure infrastructure to reduce manual reporting burden.
content_blocks.heading: Measure burden: the 15-minute visit problem
